excerpt: Powabase is a Postgres backend for AI apps with RAG, agents, auth and storage built in, open source or managed. Pricing, alternatives and launch feedback.
content:
Powabase is a backend for AI applications, pitched as "the AI-native Supabase alternative". Every project gets its own Postgres database with pgvector, plus authentication, file storage, realtime and dedicated compute. On top of that sit AI parts most AI apps end up building themselves: a document pipeline that indexes files on upload (with OCR and vector, keyword, hybrid or tree retrieval), agents and multi-agent workflows, memory, and tools over HTTP or MCP, all behind one REST API.

It is designed to be built with coding agents: there is a Powabase skill and MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode, and API guides for Replit, Lovable, v0, Base44 and Bolt.new. You can self-host the full single-project stack for free under the Apache-2.0 licence with one docker compose up, or use the managed Powabase Cloud. You can bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or OpenRouter keys or pay for AI usage from your credits.

The team on Product Hunt is led by founder Hunter Zhao, with Michael Chang, Xin Chen and Tony Zhang. Hunter says the team has run an AI development agency since ChatGPT came out. Powabase launched on Product Hunt on 27 May 2026 and finished #1 for the day with 404 upvotes and 66 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Powabase ourselves. This page brings together its official site and pricing page, its Product Hunt launch and the public pricing pages of comparable backends, and says where each fact comes from.

paragraphs: Hunter Zhao says his team has run an AI development shop since ChatGPT first came out and noticed the same pattern on client projects: nearly every AI app needs Postgres, a vector store, RAG pipelines, an agent runtime, memory, auth and file storage, usually stitched together from six to eight tools with a lot of glue code.

He says they have built about 100 production AI apps in regulated fields such as finance, insurance, education and government, and the glue was always the slowest and most expensive part, so they built Powabase to provide it as one backend.
launch_story.attribution: Hunter Zhao, founder, on Product Hunt

use_cases: Giving a coding agent a ready backend with database, auth, storage and RAG
Adding document search and question answering to an existing product
Running multi-agent workflows with logged tool calls and citations
Self-hosting an AI backend inside your own infrastructure

fit: are agencies or in-house teams building AI apps for clients
build with Claude Code, Codex, Replit, Lovable or similar tools
want Postgres underneath rather than a proprietary database
not_fit: prefer to assemble your own stack in tools like n8n or Flowise on your existing Postgres, as one commenter said
want projects to stay up on the free cloud tier without activity: inactive free projects suspend after 7 days and are deleted after 30

pricing.intro: Powabase is free to self-host. Powabase Cloud is usage-based; paid plans include a matching monthly credit balance that rolls over. Prices are in US dollars.

plans.name: Self-hosted
plans.detail: Apache-2.0; full single-project stack on your own infrastructure; bring your own LLM keys; community support on Discord

plans.name: Cloud Free
plans.detail: All platform features, $10 in free credits on sign-up, pay as you go; inactive projects suspend after 7 days and are deleted after 30

plans.name: Self Serve
plans.detail: $25 of monthly credits, any compute tier, up to 25% cheaper per-call costs and 15% cheaper compute than Free, email support

plans.name: Scale
plans.detail: $300 of monthly credits, up to 50% cheaper per-call costs and 20% cheaper compute than Free, priority live support

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Cloud, private VPC or on-premises; US/EU data residency; SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO, audit logs, SLAs

notes: Compute is billed per hour by tier; the smallest (Sandbox) costs $0.0346 an hour on the Free plan, according to the pricing page.
Unused credits roll over month to month.

alternatives.intro: Backends developers compare Powabase with (Powabase's own site lists Supabase, Firebase, Convex, Neon, Pinecone and LangChain). Prices are from each company's own pricing page on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Supabase
items.what: Open-source Postgres backend with auth, storage, realtime and pgvector
items.difference: The closest like-for-like option; Powabase adds a built-in RAG pipeline, agents and workflows on top of a similar Postgres base.

items.name: Convex
items.what: Reactive backend with database, functions, file storage and vector search
items.difference: Uses its own reactive database rather than Postgres, and has no built-in agent runtime.

liked: Treating Postgres as the foundation rather than an afterthought
Removing the 'infra glue' between six or more tools
asked: What actually saves tokens (fewer third-party frameworks for the coding agent to navigate, and agentic RAG, the founder said)
Whether it uses pgvector (yes; multimodal files are first turned into text descriptions, then indexed)
criticised: One developer said he prefers bringing his own Postgres and keeping RAG in tools like n8n or Flowise; the founder replied that each project's Postgres is a normal database with a direct connection string

quotes.text: The Postgres-native approach is interesting most RAG tooling treats the database as an afterthought rather than the foundation.
quotes.author: Florent Berrez

quotes.text: Have mixed feelings with these PostgreSQL wrappers.
quotes.author: Asher Snyder

pros: Open source and free to self-host
RAG, agents and workflows built into the backend
Skills and MCP server for popular coding agents
cons: Free cloud projects are suspended after 7 days of inactivity
Usage-based pricing takes some working out across compute tiers and per-call costs
Younger and less established than Supabase or Firebase

quotes.author: Sounak Bhattacharya
quotes.text: The "token-efficient" claim is the one I'd want unpacked
quotes.reply: Hunter Zhao said a coding agent relies much less on gluing frameworks and packages together because Powabase's parts work together out of the box, and its agentic RAG saves tokens at run time.

x.none: We found no posts about Powabase on X yet.

faq.a: A Postgres backend for AI apps: each project gets a database with pgvector, auth, storage, realtime and compute, plus built-in RAG, agents, workflows and MCP tools behind one REST API.

Self-hosting is free under Apache-2.0. Powabase Cloud has a free tier with $10 of sign-up credit, Self Serve at $25 a month, Scale at $300 a month and custom Enterprise plans; paid plans include matching credits that roll over.
Yes. The self-hosted edition is Apache-2.0 and runs with one docker compose up, according to its pricing page.

faq.q: Can I bring my own AI keys?
faq.a: Yes: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and OpenRouter keys are stored per project and encrypted, or you can pay for inference from your credits.
Yes, the founder confirmed it on Product Hunt.

faq.q: How is Powabase different from Supabase?
faq.a: Both are Postgres backends with auth and storage. Powabase adds a built-in RAG pipeline, agents and workflows aimed at AI apps.
